report.summary: Reviewed chunk 8 of 11 of gated_writes.py. Found _promote_one, _promote_one_inner (referenced), promote_candidates, _promote_locked. Claims about reset/clean, catch-all, order, never raises, cancellation handling are checked.
risks: line 846 | medium | git reset --hard and clean -fd run unconditionally after any exception in _promote_one_inner; if that exception was due to a bug, the reset may mask it. | Check if there is any logging or monitoring of the reset/clean actions.

handoff.purpose: Defines _promote_one (catch-all wrapper), promote_candidates (Phase 2 entry point), and _promote_locked (creates integration worktree).

symbols.name: _promote_one
symbols.note: Wraps _promote_one_inner with a catch-all exception handler; returns refusal dict on any exception.

symbols.name: promote_candidates
symbols.note: Phase 2 entry: acquires lock, calls _promote_locked, handles PromotionUnavailable. Returns dict with 'promoted', 'refused', 'not_gated'.

symbols.name: _promote_locked
symbols.note: Creates integration worktree from base_commit, initializes _PinnedWorktreeGit. Called under lock.

claims.text: Whatever partial state add/commit/gate left behind, the integration worktree must come back to EXACTLY current_head with a clean tree before the NEXT candidate's staleness check above runs -- otherwise that check is comparing against a lie.
claims.why: The code at lines 846-847 runs git reset --hard current_head and git clean -fd unconditionally after any exception in the try block, restoring clean state. This matches the claim.

claims.text: ``_promote_one_inner`` already resets the integration worktree to ``current_head`` on any failure it anticipates; this is the net under that for the failures it does not.
claims.why: The code for _promote_one_inner is not in this chunk; the claim about its behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Never raises: every failure mode (lock unavailable, apply refused, cumulative gate failed, base moved and the retry also failed) is a refusal in the returned report, not an exception.
claims.why: The function promote_candidates has a try/except that only catches PromotionUnavailable. If _PromotionLock raises any other exception (e.g., OSError), it will propagate up, violating the 'never raises' claim. The claim is not fully satisfied by this code alone.

claims.text: ``cancel`` is forwarded to every STALENESS-triggered regeneration (``_reattempt``'s own ``TaskAttempt`` -- see ``gate_candidates``' docstring for what it accepts) AND to the cumulative re-gate's own ``command_gate`` call inside ``_promote_one_inner``
claims.why: The forwarding to _reattempt and command_gate is not visible in this chunk; it would be inside _promote_one_inner which is not included.

claims.text: the SAME unconditional ``git reset --hard``/``clean -fd`` that already runs for a genuine cumulative-gate failure also runs for a cancelled one
claims.why: The handling of cancellation inside _promote_one_inner is not shown; the reset/clean code seen (lines 846-847) runs only after exceptions in the try block of _promote_one_inner, but the cancellation mechanism is not detailed here.

claims.text: Filtered by object IDENTITY, not dataclass equality: two distinct candidates can legitimately compare equal on fields.
claims.why: The code uses `id(c)` to build the set `live_ids` and then checks `id(c) not in live_ids` at line 903, which is identity-based filtering.

claims.text: Reported, not dropped: a candidate that never reached STATE_CLEAN in Phase 1 (escalated, gates_failed, no_change, ...) has nothing to promote, but silently omitting it here would make this report LOOK complete while actually only covering a subset of what was asked -- the same 'silent partial result' shape this whole module exists to refuse elsewhere.
claims.why: The code builds `not_gated` list for candidates whose id is not in `live_ids` (i.e., not gated) and includes it in the final report at line 917. So non-gated candidates are reported, not dropped.

claims.text: ``candidates`` is what Phase 1 (``gate_candidates``) returned, in the SAME order they were submitted -- that order is promotion order too
claims.why: The order of promotion is determined by the iteration over `live` (line 904), which preserves the order of `candidates` after filtering. The claim about Phase 1 returning the same order is not verifiable here.

observations.what: The reset/clean commands at lines 846-847 use check=False, so failures are ignored. This matches the claim of unconditional cleanup.
The docstring of promote_candidates claims 'Never raises', but the try/except only catches PromotionUnavailable. Other exceptions from _PromotionLock (e.g., OSError) would propagate.
promote_candidates returns a dict with keys 'promoted', 'refused', 'not_gated', and 'integration_branch'. The return type is not enforced; callers may expect different structure.

The variable `live` is built by checking `getattr(c.result, 'ok', False) and c.result.artifact and not c.result.artifact.is_empty`. This assumes c.result has 'ok' and 'artifact' attributes; if not, getattr returns False and candidate is excluded.
The integration branch name uses uuid.uuid4().hex[:10] (10 hex chars). This is not guaranteed to be unique, but collisions are extremely unlikely.
_promote_locked calls manager.create_worktree and then checks git.admin_dir is None. If admin_dir is None, it attempts cleanup. This suggests create_worktree may not raise on failure.
